title: First-byte surge and tokens/sec drop — rapid throughput recovery across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Ava Morgan
description:
Summary: Several large customers reported sudden regressions in initial-response latency (first-byte) accompanied by a measurable drop in tokens/sec across hosted and dedicated clusters. Impacted workloads are mixed-length chat and long-generation pipelines using LlamaX-13B and a 70B research model variant. Symptoms started after the runtime 1.19 kernel selector change that introduced a new multi-tenant coalescing path and a revised KV cache eviction timing.

Observed behavior:
- TTFT increased by 120-350ms for median and 400-1,200ms for p95 on affected routes.
- Sustained tokens/sec throughput dropped 20-40% under steady load on dedicated pools using shared GPU nodes.
- Errors were rare; majority is increased queuing and delayed KV cache warm-up causing long first-token stalls.

Why urgent: High-value customers (two enterprise accounts on Dedicated and three Hosted customers) opened escalations citing SLA misses and customer-facing latency spikes. We prioritized immediate mitigations while continuing root-cause work.
timeline: 2025-03-10 09:12 - Alert: distributed tracing and console TTFT dashboards showed correlated first-byte spikes across regions
2025-03-10 10:30 - Triage call with on-call infra, runtime, and SRE teams. Identified recent rollout of kernel-selector v1.19.2 and coalescing-enabled flag flips as common change
2025-03-10 14:00 - Applied short-term routing toggle to disable multi-tenant coalescing for high-priority pools (hosted,dedicated) - measurable improvement for one customer (p95 down 30%)

2025-03-11 02:25 - Deployed hotfix 'adaptive-kv-hysteresis' to increase KV retention window by 60% for model families with long prefix distributions. Mixed results: reduced cold-start stalls but produced scheduling backpressure on smaller pools
2025-03-11 11:05 - Rolled back adaptive-kv-hysteresis due to a tokens/sec regression in throughput tests for 70B variant in dedicated environment

2025-03-12 03:40 - Implemented per-model QPS shaper + prioritized fast-path for pinned customers (canary). Applied to two enterprise tenants; early traces show p50 TTFT improvement 180ms, tokens/sec restored to 95% baseline
2025-03-12 09:00 - Ongoing: collecting telemetry across regions and scheduled targeted load tests for 70B variant to validate kernel heuristics and KV cache sizing
root_cause_analysis: Primary drivers: interaction between new kernel-selector coalescing heuristics and aggressive KV cache eviction. For mixed-length workloads, coalescing delayed per-request fast-path selection, forcing some requests into a heavier kernel with cold KV cache state.
Secondary factor: scheduling preemption window (conductor) was too short for large-model KV priming, causing repeated cache churn under bursty traffic.
Contributing: a recent default change to the batching window aimed at throughput improved average cost but increased variance for first-token latency on non-uniform length distributions.
decisions: Short-term: keep multi-tenant coalescing disabled for Dedicated pools with SLA customers until further validation
Immediate mitigation: per-model QPS shaper to reduce head-of-line entanglement and ensure KV priming completes before preemption
Long-term: expand kernel-selector tests to include mixed-length synthetic traces and add KV eviction stress tests to CI
Fallback policy: route traffic to a KV-optimized model variant (quantized 4-bit profile) when latency SLOs are at risk
mitigations_applied: Routing toggle: disable coalescing for flagged pools (rolled out 2025-03-10)
Canary per-model QPS shaper & priority fast-path (deployed 2025-03-12 to two enterprise tenants)
Temporary reduced preemption aggressiveness in conductor (applied to dedicated-only clusters)
Rollback of adaptive-kv-hysteresis after negative throughput regression (2025-03-11)
next_steps: Complete extended load tests for 70B variant across dedicated pool sizes (owner: Diego Ramos) - target 2025-03-14
Add KV eviction/priming scenarios to the runtime regression suite and gate future kernel-selector rollouts (owner: Runtime QA)
Build a lightweight telemetry signal for early first-byte surge detection and include auto-toggle in Console (owner: Observability)
Prepare release candidate runtime-1.20.1 with tuned coalescing thresholds and improved conductor timings
Follow-up postmortem and customer-facing incident summary (owner: SRE/Support)
